body.statement:
Let \(q=|\mathcal I|\), let \(p=nN\), and let \(\lambda\geq1\) be the rational bit length of the labeled graph and intervention input.  There is a terminating exact compiler for both directed cover relations.  It first produces the finite pivot-chart formulas for \(\mathcal D_G\) and \(\mathcal D_H\), then enumerates visible-source subsets and surjections, clears only the nonzero pivot and intervention determinants in the proportionality and simultaneous-response equations, and applies effective sign-condition block elimination to the resulting \(\forall C\,\exists(D,a)\) sentence.  With
\[
s=(q+N+1)2^{8N^2},\quad d=4N^3,\quad \tau=(\lambda+1)2^{8N^2},
\]
and with the absolute effective constant \(c_{\mathrm{qe}}\) of the cited elimination theorem, one directed decision, including a finite sign-cell certificate, uses at most
\[
\mathsf B(N,q,\lambda)
=(\tau+1)^2(s+1)^{(p+1)(p+N+1)+1}
(d+1)^{c_{\mathrm{qe}}(p+1)(p+N+1)}                                   \tag{16}
\]
bit operations.  Hence comparison uses at most \(2\mathsf B(N,q,\lambda)\) bit operations.  Exhaustive enumeration of the equivalence class modulo latent relabeling terminates within
\[
2^{N(N-1)}\bigl(2\mathsf B(N,q,\lambda)+\ell!\,N^2\bigr)               \tag{17}
\]
bit operations, apart from a fixed linear-time encoding overhead.  The certificates and bounds cover forced zeros, punctured fibers, Hall--Rado failures, nullification, and all lower-dimensional incidences; the compiler contains no structural-coefficient or source-law quantifier.
body.proof_tex:
We construct the advertised formula before invoking elimination.  A rank equality for a matrix with at most \(N\) rows and columns is a finite disjunction over its possible rank: a chosen pivot minor is nonzero and every larger minor vanishes.  Applying this to every local system in Definition \(\texttt{def:exact-mixing-domain}\), Gaussian elimination on a chosen pivot chart writes an affine base point and a basis of the direction space of each fiber \(\mathcal A_j(C)\) as rational functions of \(C\).  The only denominators are the selected nonzero minors.  Adjoining the base point gives a rational spanning family for \(W_j(C)\).  Therefore each Hall--Rado inequality is the finite minor condition
\[
 \operatorname{rank}[W_j(C):j\in J]\geq |J|,
 \qquad J\subseteq L.
\]
Clearing the chart denominators does not change the condition on a chart.  The punctured-coordinate requirements and intervention principal minors are likewise Boolean combinations of polynomial equalities and strict inequalities.  Theorem \(\texttt{thm:exact-mixing-realization}\) proves that the resulting quantifier-free formula \(\operatorname{Dom}_G(C)\) defines exactly \(\mathcal D_G\), including all singular and lower-dimensional chart intersections.

For visible sets \(U,W\subseteq V\) and a surjection \(f:U\twoheadrightarrow W\), introduce at most \(N\) scalars \(a_i\) and impose
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &C_{:,i}=0\Longleftrightarrow i\notin U,
 &&D_{:,j}=0\Longleftrightarrow j\notin W,\\
 &a_i\ne0,
 &&C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\quad(i\in U).                                \tag{17}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Column nonzeroness is the strict polynomial inequality \(\sum_{r\in X}C_{ri}^2>0\).  On the domain charts, response equality is polynomialized without an inverse as
\[
 C_{O,S}\operatorname{adj}(C_{S,S})\det(D_{S,S})
 =D_{O,S}\operatorname{adj}(D_{S,S})\det(C_{S,S}),
 \qquad O=X\setminus S.                                                \tag{18}
\]
Both determinants are nonzero on the domain, so (18) is equivalent to \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\).

Let \(\Theta_f(C,D,a)\) conjoin \(\operatorname{Dom}_H(D)\), (17), and (18) for all \(S\in\mathcal I\).  The directed compiler decides
\[
 \forall C\in\mathbb R^{n\times N}\;
 \left[
 \operatorname{Dom}_G(C)\Longrightarrow
 \bigvee_{U,W,f}\exists D\in\mathbb R^{n\times N}
 \exists a\in\mathbb R^U\;\Theta_f(C,D,a)
 \right].                                                              \tag{19}
\]
By Definition \(\texttt{def:directed-chart-cover}\), (19) is precisely \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\); Theorem \(\texttt{thm:coupled-equivalence}\) then makes it equivalent to directed response-kernel containment.  The source-distribution quantifier has already been eliminated by Theorem \(\texttt{thm:unrestricted-source-partition-containment}\), and the structural matrix \(B\) by exact mixing realization.  Thus real-algebraic elimination is applied to the new finite chart representation, not to the original mechanism-existence problem.

We verify the stated size bounds.  Every local or pivot matrix has at most \(N\) rows and columns and hence at most \(2^{2N}\) minors.  Choosing pivot data for at most \(N\) local systems produces at most \(2^{2N^2}\) joint charts.  A concatenated Hall matrix has at most \(N\) rows and \(N^2\) columns and fewer than \(2^{N+N^2}\) minors.  The \(2^\ell\) Hall subfamilies, \(q\) intervention blocks, and zero-pattern clauses fit within \((q+N+1)2^{4N^2}\) additional recorded atoms.  Finally, the number of pairs of visible subsets and partial source maps is at most
\[
 2^{2N}(N+1)^N\leq2^{3N^2}\qquad(N\geq2).
\]
Sharing repeated atoms gives the conservative total
\[
 s=(q+N+1)2^{8N^2}.
\]
Pivot denominators are minors of degree at most \(N\); a Hall minor uses at most \(N\) rational entries, and clearing at most \(N\) denominators leaves degree below \(d=4N^3\).  Equations (17)--(18) have smaller degree.  Expanding the fewer than \(2^{8N^2}\) recorded determinant atoms by the Leibniz formula bounds the integer coefficient bit length by
\[
 \tau=(\lambda+1)2^{8N^2}.
\]
These bounds include empty blocks and zero signs.

Formula (19) has two real quantifier blocks, of sizes at most \(p=nN\) and \(p+N\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:effective-real-quantifier-elimination}\) therefore gives
\[
 (\tau+1)^2(s+1)^{(p+1)(p+N+1)+1}
 (d+1)^{c_{\mathrm{qe}}(p+1)(p+N+1)}
 =\mathsf B(N,q,\lambda)
\]
bit operations after the one advertised enlargement of the absolute constant.  Its sign conditions and algebraic sample encodings form a finite certificate.  Zero signs are retained, so the certificate includes forced zeros, nullification, Hall--Rado failures, and lower-dimensional cells.  Running the decision in both directions proves the comparison bound.

There are \(2^{N(N-1)}\) labeled loopless digraphs.  For each candidate, perform the two directed decisions.  To quotient only latent relabeling, compute the least adjacency encoding under the \(\ell!\) simultaneous row-and-column permutations fixing every observed label, at cost at most \(\ell!N^2\).  This proves the enumeration bound, termination, and completeness, with no centering or moment premise.
body.justification: The theorem turns the exact-support invariant into a terminating certificate-producing decision and enumeration procedure with an explicit finite bit bound.
body.consumer: Finite graph searches can be globally certified even on forced-zero, rank-deficient, and cancellation strata.
